A growing child is not typically expected to experience a sternal (breastbone) fracture due to trauma. However, sternal fractures can occur in this age group due to typical age-related traumatic incidents.

Sternal fractures are relatively rare in children, but they can be an important diagnosis to rule out. Ultrasonography is often used as a diagnostic tool for fracture detection, while radiography (X-rays) provides visualization of the extent of the dislocation.

In cases where sternal fractures are suspected, it's essential to consider alternative diagnoses and rule out other conditions that may cause similar symptoms. If you suspect your child has a sternal fracture, consult with a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and treatment.

It's also worth noting that while sternal fractures in children can be rare, they do require attention and prompt care to ensure proper healing and minimize complications.
